page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-32 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 60.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for its disk requirements.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4d-highcpu-32 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, particularly in stress-ng CPU tests and single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3. Multi-threaded decompression and PassMark CPU tests, including encryption and physics simulations, rank in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks fall into the average tier. The instance also shows strong capabilities in static web serving and small-model LLM text generation, while medium-model LLM inference and database operations perform at average levels.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers high compute density but presents a clear tradeoff with its limited memory allocation and lack of local NVMe storage. This makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or high-speed local disk I/O. Appropriate workloads include single-threaded or moderately parallelized compute tasks, static web serving, cryptography, and lightweight machine learning inference.
